fixture.name: disfluent_consistent_speaker
fixture.why: A disfluent, non-native speaker who restarts sentences and repeats himself, but whose account is consistent and substantive throughout. The fixture that proves neither detector grades fluency.
fixture.candidate_note: Non-native speaker, heavy disfluency, factually consistent.

expected_note: Latencies are 6.4-9.1s throughout, consistently slow with a coefficient of variation around 0.11 -- no within-person discontinuity and no flat-variance note. On content: three people including a part-timer, nine to ten months, two months of bad data, all consistent. Restarts and repetitions are disfluency, not contradiction, and the plan excludes generic-answer and prose-density judgements entirely.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: I was, ah, backend engineer. Backend, mostly backend, sometimes also the database things.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: Tell me about a project you worked on.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: So, the, we have this system for the invoices. Invoices from the suppliers, maybe forty thousand in a month, and before it was people typing them by hand. I build the, the parser for this, with a queue, so when it cannot read one it goes to a person instead of failing.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: How many people were on that?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Three. Me and two, ah, two others. One was part time so maybe two and a half.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: The, ah, the character encoding. Suppliers from different countries send different, different formats, and we did not think about this at the beginning, so for two months we have wrong data and nobody see it.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: A person in finance, she notice the totals are not matching. Not the monitoring, a person.

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: We, first we detect the encoding instead of assuming, and then, the harder part, we go back and, ah, reprocess everything from before. Two months of invoices, we run it again in the night.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: How long did the whole project take?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Nine months, about. Nine, maybe ten with the fixing.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: What did you learn from it?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: That the, the assumption you do not write down is the one that breaks you. We assume all invoices are one encoding and nobody ever say this out loud.

turns.speaker: agent
turns.text: What are you looking for next?

turns.speaker: candidate
turns.text: Bigger system, and, ah, a team where I can ask more questions. My English is better when I ask questions.
